newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen GDP up 16.5 pct yr/yr in first half.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen GDP up 16.5 pct yr/yr in first half.

text.p: Gross domestic product growth (GDP) in southern China's boom town of Shenzhen soared 16.5 percent year-on-year to 46.332 billion yuan in the first half of 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Monday.
That growth rate far outpaced first-quarter national GDP, which registered 9.4 percent growth.
The national figure for the first half of 1997 has yet to be announced.
Retail price inflation in the first half was less than the 3.3 percent target set for the year, the newspaper said but gave no exact figure.

The special economic zone's industrial output value reached 60.334 billion yuan in the period, up 7.6 billion yuan compared with the first half of 1996, the newspaper said, quoting figures released by the city's statistical bureau.
Fixed asset investment in Shenzhen, which borders on the former British colony of Hong Kong, jumped 22.3 percent year-on-year to 14.718 billion yuan in the first six months, it said.
Foreign trade increased 14.3 percent to 20.212 billion yuan and actual foreign investment surged 50 percent to US$1.352 billion in the first half of this year, the newspaper said.
The city government's budgetary fiscal income rose 33.4 percent in the first half, reaching 6.947 billion yuan, it said.
Shenzhen, China's first special economic zone, has been at the forefront of China's economic reform since the late 1970s.
